worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice reduced the expected burden from alternative regulation to 2. With the proposal cost at 6, continued support now yields -4 under SA. The coalition therefore decided not to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition is withdrawing its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that withdrawals following private notices will be preceded by internal documents revising expected alternative-regulation burdens downward, rather than merely revising competitive benefits.
worlds.derivation: Under SA, support depends jointly on the alternative-regulation burden and the proposal cost; the notice can change either benefit, but only a burden revision changes the SA payoff. The generated withdrawal makes the predicted documentary distinction especially observable.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal archives preserve dated assessments sufficiently close to the decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2 but left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Under SA, the relevant payoff remains 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that some internal records will report sharply worsened competitive calculations without a corresponding withdrawal of support when the assessed burden from alternative regulation remains high.
worlds.derivation: The notice process can reduce competitive benefit while leaving regulatory burden unchanged, and SA makes support depend on the latter net of proposal cost. Together these premises imply possible divergence between commercial assessments and support decisions.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal documents record both commercial assessments and policy decisions.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. The expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. Because SA evaluates continued support as 12 minus 6, the payoff is 6. The coalition decided to maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition remains supportive of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Across archived cases, researchers should predict a stronger association between support changes and revised alternative-regulation estimates than between support changes and revised competitive-benefit estimates.
worlds.derivation: Notices alter either estimate with equal probability, while SA maps only the alternative-regulation burden, net of the common cost, into the support decision. Decision reversals and public communication errors add noise but do not erase the expected association.
worlds.extra_assumption: A sufficiently large comparable archive permits the two kinds of revisions to be coded reliably.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice lowered the expected alternative-regulation burden to 2. After subtracting the proposal cost of 6, continued support has a payoff of -4 under SA. The coalition decided to end its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict occasional conflicts between internal decision records and public statements, with later internal correspondence treating the public statement as a communication error rather than evidence of a different payoff calculation.
worlds.derivation: The decision follows the SA payoff subject to a decision-reversal probability, while the public note separately has an independent probability of reporting the opposite decision. Jointly, these premises generate documentary discrepancies unrelated to the private calculation.
worlds.extra_assumption: Subsequent internal correspondence discusses or corrects material public misstatements.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice revised the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2. The proposal still costs 6, producing a continued-support payoff of -4 under SA. The coalition decided not to continue its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal withdrawal records will cluster immediately after documented downward revisions that move the expected alternative-regulation burden below the proposal cost.
worlds.derivation: SA defines payoff as burden minus cost, and the coalition normally follows the payoff sign after receiving the notice. Combining the threshold rule with dated notices implies a temporal and threshold pattern in internal documents.
worlds.extra_assumption: Documents record sufficiently precise dates and burden estimates to identify threshold crossings.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2, while the expected alternative-regulation burden stayed at 12. Under SA, continued support yields 12 minus 6, or 6. The coalition decided to retain its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition will continue supporting the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal justifications for continued support emphasize avoided alternative-regulation burdens even when contemporaneous commercial analyses become substantially less favorable.
worlds.derivation: The notice can worsen the competitive calculation without changing the regulatory burden, while SA bases support on the regulatory burden net of cost. These premises jointly predict a separation between commercial pessimism and the stated internal rationale for support.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal memoranda explain decisions rather than recording only their outcomes.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit to 2 but left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. The SA payoff from support is therefore 6 after the proposal cost. Despite that positive calculation, the coalition decided not to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition is ending its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict rare internal decisions that contradict the recorded sign of the SA payoff, without a preceding change in the alternative-regulation estimate.
worlds.derivation: A competitive-benefit notice leaves the positive SA payoff unchanged, but the independent decision-reversal rule can produce non-support. Together, these premises imply infrequent documentary exceptions to the usual payoff-decision relationship.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal records preserve the payoff assessment made before the decision reversal.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice reduced the expected burden of alternative regulation to 2. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 gives a continued-support payoff of -4 under SA. The coalition decided to withdraw support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has withdrawn support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that documents preceding withdrawal contain revised expectations about alternative regulatory pressure, while documents about competitive positioning alone have weaker predictive value for withdrawal.
worlds.derivation: SA makes alternative-regulation burden, not competitive benefit, determinative after subtracting the common proposal cost. Combining this rule with the two possible private notices yields different expected documentary precursors to withdrawal.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can distinguish assessments of regulatory pressure from assessments of competitive positioning.
